questions.q: What are the five poetic forms (नननन) used in Tulsidas's works as discussed in Chapter 7, and which form has 31-31 characters per line with a pause at the 16th character?
questions.a: The five forms are: दोहा (doha), चौपाई (chaupai), सवैया (savaiya), कवित्त (kavitt), and सोरठा (soratha). The दोहा (doha) has 31-31 characters per line with a pause at the 16th character. A wrong answer (e.g., naming "कवित्त" for the 31-character form) reveals the student hasn't internalized the metrical distinctions taught in the chapter's "छंद परिचय" section — they're confusing the fixed-meter doha with the variable-meter kavitt.

questions.q: In the discussion question "सीता के वियोग में राम का जो शोक है, उसे कवि ने हनुमान के मुख से व्यक्त किया है" — why does the poet choose Hanuman as the speaker rather than Ram himself? Explain using the concept of "लोकमंगल" (public welfare).
questions.a: Tulsidas uses Hanuman as the speaker because Hanuman embodies devoted service (सेवा) and witness (साक्षी) — making Ram's grief relatable to common people (लोक) rather than presenting it as divine play (लीला). This serves लोकमंगल by showing that even God feels separation, validating human suffering. A wrong answer focusing only on "Hanuman is Ram's devotee" misses the pedagogical function: the poet mediates divine experience through a human-accessible voice to achieve social harmony (सामाजिक समरसता).

questions.q: During a discussion, a peer claims: "तुलसीदास ने केवल धार्मिक भक्ति लिखी, सामाजिक सुधार नहीं।" Using the नखशिख वर्णन in the first poem (फूल-चुनि फूलकु...), construct a 3-sentence oral rebuttal that cites specific imagery.
questions.a: "तुलसीदास ने पहले पद में 'फूल-चुनि फूलकु' के माध्यम से श्रमजीवी वर्ग (माली, किसान) का चित्रण किया है जो राजमहल के लिए फूल चुनते हैं — यह वर्ग-संवेदनशीलता है। दूसरे पद में 'केवट' और 'शबरी' के प्रसंग सामाजिक भेदभाव तोड़ते हैं। तीसरे पद में 'कौन दगाबाज' कहकर सामाजिक विश्वासघात पर प्रश्न उठाया गया है — यह केवल भक्ति नहीं, लोकजागरण है।" A weak rebuttal would quote without explaining the social class implications of each image.

questions.q: Compare the discussion dynamics when analyzing a दोहा (closed form, 2 lines) versus a सवैया (open form, 4 lines with 13/11 meter). How does the poetic structure change the type of evidence you cite and the depth of interpretation possible in a 2-minute speaking turn?
questions.a: A दोहा discussion focuses on compression — you cite the exact 31-character line, explain the metaphor's density (e.g., "सीतल सीतल..."), and conclude quickly. A सवैया allows narrative development — you trace the 4-line argument (e.g., Ram's grief → Hanuman's observation → philosophical conclusion → devotional appeal), citing line-by-line progression. The दोहा demands precision; the सवैया demands synthesis. Students who treat both identically miss how form shapes analytical approach.

questions.q: Evaluate this discussion strategy: "I'll wait for others to speak first, then agree with the strongest point and add one quote." Is this effective for CBSE Speaking Assessment criteria? Justify with reference to "initiative," "evidence use," and "collaborative building."
questions.a: This strategy scores low on "initiative" (CBSE expects initiating at least once) and "collaborative building" (mere agreement isn't building — extending, questioning, or synthesizing is). It partially meets "evidence use" but reactively. An effective strategy: initiate with a focused interpretive question ("How does the soratha form in the third poem reflect social fragmentation?"), cite evidence when others respond, then synthesize: "Combining Priya's point on meter and Rohan's on imagery, the soratha's asymmetry mirrors the social imbalance Tulsidas critiques." This demonstrates all three criteria.

questions.q: Create a 90-second opening statement for a discussion on: "तुलसीदास का 'राम' केवल धार्मिक आदर्श नहीं, सामाजिक न्याय का प्रतीक है।" Use at least three distinct textual references from different poetic forms in the chapter.
questions.a: A strong opening: "तुलसीदास के राम तीन रूपों में सामाजिक न्याय के प्रतीक हैं: पहले, दोहा 'सीतल सीतल...' में वे शबरी के जूठे बेर खाकर जाति-भेद तोड़ते हैं। दूसरे, सवैया 'कौन दगाबाज...' में वे सामाजिक विश्वासघात को दैवीय न्याय से जोड़ते हैं। तीसरे, सोरठा 'हनुमान के वचन...' में वे शोक को लोक-सुलभ बनाते हैं — राजा नहीं, सेवक बोलता है। ये तीनों छंद-रूप मिलकर दिखाते हैं कि राम की मर्यादा सामाजिक समता की मर्यादा है।" A weak opening lists quotes without the unifying "social justice" thesis or uses only one poetic form.
